evals.prompt: I have Python available through uv on macOS. Convert ./papers/demo.pdf to ./papers/demo.md with MinerU lightweight, save a manifest, and avoid adding requests as a dependency.
evals.expected_output: Chooses the bundled Python helper as the primary path, runs it with uv run, uses --mode file, saves Markdown to ./papers/demo.md, writes or mentions the .mineru.json manifest, and notes that the helper uses stdlib/minimal signed PUT rather than requests.

evals.prompt: I am on Windows and cannot rely on Python being installed. Show me how to parse a local .\slides.pptx through MinerU lightweight and save .\slides.md.
evals.expected_output: Chooses native PowerShell as the no-Python Windows fallback, uses Invoke-RestMethod for /parse/file, uploads with Invoke-WebRequest -Method Put -InFile or curl.exe -T fallback, polls /parse/{task_id}, and downloads markdown_url to .\slides.md.

evals.prompt: On a minimal Linux box I only have curl, no jq and no Python. I need to submit a public PDF URL to MinerU and get the Markdown link.
evals.expected_output: Provides a dependency-free curl workflow, saves submit/poll JSON responses to files, tells the user to manually copy data.task_id and data.markdown_url, avoids pretending JSON extraction is fully automated without jq/Python, and uses no Authorization header.

evals.prompt: MinerU file mode gave me a task_id and file_url, but upload failed with Aliyun OSS 403 SignatureDoesNotMatch. What is the fastest fix if I used a form-style upload client?
evals.expected_output: Identifies the upload step as the failure point, explains that accidental Content-Type or form upload behavior can invalidate the signed URL, recommends retrying the existing file_url with the Python helper/minimal http.client PUT or curl -T, and says not to repeatedly resubmit /parse/file unless the URL expired.

evals.prompt: Convert every PDF under ./course into Markdown under ./md. Python is available, but some PDFs are 42 pages and several folders contain files named slides.pdf.
evals.expected_output: Uses the Python helper in a client-side loop, preserves source folder layout under ./md to avoid basename collisions, chunks long PDFs into <=20-page page_range requests such as 1-20/21-40/41-42, merges chunks in order with optional page markers, and writes a manifest with per-file status.
